name: post_update
description: Post a short progress update in this conversation's Slack thread.

name: ask
description: Ask the person a question when the request itself is unclear. Their reply arrives as your next message, so end your turn after asking.

name: react
description: Add an emoji reaction to the message you are answering.

name: post_files
description: Post files from your session folder (screenshots, videos, reports) to this conversation's Slack thread, with one line of text.

name: track_task
description: Record that this conversation is now a piece of work (for status, Linear and metrics). kind: feature, bug or chore.

name: finish_task
description: Mark this conversation's task done, with its outcome (a PR link, say).

name: start_task
description: Start a separate session for a piece of work, with a self-contained brief, to split one request into parallel tasks.

name: spawn_agent
description: Start a spawned agent: a separate session that works on its own after your turn and reports back later in a new turn here. Returns its id at once. When it finishes, its final message arrives in this conversation as an <agent-notification> and starts a new turn here if you've ended yours, so don't wait for it. Background agents (the Agent tool with run_in_background) keep your session open instead, and your reply posts when they finish. The brief must be self-contained: the agent doesn't see this conversation. At most 3 per conversation and 4 overall run at once, and one that fails isn't retried. cwd: the directory it works in (relative to your folder, or absolute); by default its own new folder. A cwd in your folder (a clone of yours) shares that checkout with you: only do that when you want it to work on your checkout, and don't change the same files meanwhile.

name: status
description: What is running and queued, whether the agent is paused, and how much of its 5-hour window this session's account has used.

name: list_tasks
description: List tasks, optionally by status or project.

name: get_task
description: Show one task.

name: cancel_task
description: Cancel a task and anything running for it.

name: stop_all
description: Stop everything: pause new work and cancel what is running. Only an admin can resume.

name: resume_all
description: Resume after stop_all.

name: read_thread
description: Read this conversation's Slack thread, or in a DM chat its messages so far (oldest first).

name: slack_read
description: Read from Slack with core's bot token: one Web API call, with params as Slack documents them. Methods: conversations.history, conversations.replies, conversations.list, conversations.info, users.info, users.list, pins.list, bookmarks.list. Replies over 20000 characters are cut; page with limit and cursor.

name: gh_prs
description: List the project's pull requests (state: open, closed or all).

name: gh_checks
description: CI check runs for a commit or branch.

name: gh_ci_log
description: The tail of a GitHub Actions job's log.

name: gh_issue
description: A GitHub issue with its comments.

name: gh_file
description: A file from the GitHub repo at a ref (default: the default branch).

name: kpis
description: The agent's own KPIs over the last `days` days (default 7): tasks by project, time per task, the share finished, PRs merged and Linear issues closed, and its tokens by project (also today, 7 days and this month, with the apps' metered model calls by upstream, and per day for the last 7 days).

name: start_project
description: Register this conversation as the build of a long project, so every session sees it and can pass it changes.

name: finish_project
description: Mark a long project done.

name: tell_project
description: Pass a change or a question to a project's build. It arrives as a message from the person you're talking to.

name: linear_install
description: Send yourself the link that installs the agent as a Linear app, so people can delegate issues to it.

name: park
description: Park this conversation until a time, then end your turn: core carries it on by itself at that time, in a new turn of this same conversation with your note, and a person's reply in the thread resumes it earlier. Use it to wait out the 5-hour soft cap when every account is over it (see status) or when someone asks you to pause until a time, instead of keeping the turn alive. until: HH:MM in the team's timezone (the next one), or an ISO date-time; leave it out to wait until an account has room again (it refuses while one is under its cap). note: what you were doing and what's next, for the turn that carries on. Core posts nothing: tell the thread yourself if it should know.

name: keep_running
description: Keep something you run up past its usual stop, or set when it stops. Without this, your container for this conversation stops 24 hours after the conversation's last message (an hour after it, if nothing runs in it), and every server in it stops with it; a service in services.toml runs until it is removed; a stack in your own Docker runs until someone stops it. what: "container" (this conversation's), "server" (the one listening on `port` in this conversation's container: it holds the container up, and once the container is past its usual stop everything else in it is stopped), "service" (`name` in services.toml: removed from the file then), "stack" (`name`, a compose project in your own Docker: stopped then). Give `hours` from now, `forever` (until someone changes it), or `clear` (back to the usual rules). Use it when someone asks for a demo or server to stay up, and say until when. People see and change all of these on the dashboard's Containers page.
